name: Gie Yong Bio Temple
description: Gie Yong Bio Temple is a temple built in the 18th century by the people of Lasem. Inside this temple, a small statue monument was also built depicting a native who became one of the 3 leaders of the Lasem Yellow War. This building serves as evidence that the Yellow War in Lasem became one of the factors in forming harmony between the Javanese and Chinese ethnicities.
location: Kelenteng Gie Yong Bio, Jalan Raya Rembang - Lasem, Babagan, Rembang, Central Java, Java, 59271, Indonesia

name: Panji Margono Statue at Gie Yong Bio Temple
description: The statue of Raden Mas Panji Margono, which was built inside the Gie Yong Bio Temple building and aligned with the statues of gods, serves as evidence of the important role of the Javanese ethnicity in the Lasem Yellow War, as well as proof that the Chinese community in Lasem highly respects the relationship between the Javanese and Chinese ethnicities in Lasem.

description: Judging from its location, the Babagan River is located on the western outskirts of Lasem. Historically, the function of a river is as a natural fortress of a region. name: Oei Ing Kyat Tomb
description: Oei Ing Kiat's tomb is located at the peak of a mountain on the outskirts of Lasem. Oei Ing Kiat was a Chinese-descendant Muslim who became a central figure in the Yellow War (1741-1743). During the war, he organized Chinese and Javanese troops, as well as Islamic boarding school students (santri), to attack the Dutch colonizers. The struggle against the colonizers was continued by Oei Ing Kiat until the end of his life in 1750.

name: Opa Jun's House
description: Opa Jun's House is a well-known place among travelers. This building was once a filming location for a wide-screen movie. Located in Babagan Village, this house features a typical Indochinese architectural design, with a colonial-style roof, Chinese-patterned building structures, and a terrace that incorporates traditional Javanese elements. Generally, the floors of Indochinese-style houses in the area use terracotta materials. In the past, this type of terracotta was usually imported directly from China. Today, similar materials can be obtained from several manufacturers located in Yogyakarta. - Kesengsem Lasem
